title: Synthetic pediatric DKA initial assessment
text: Educational fixture only. Pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis is treated as a high-acuity presentation requiring immediate clinician assessment and use of an approved current institutional protocol. The initial record should include presenting symptoms, relevant diabetes history, recent illness, weight, vital signs, hydration findings, neurological status, glucose, electrolytes, venous blood gas, and ketones. The team confirms patient identity, specimen times, allergies, vascular access status, and whether senior pediatric and critical-care review has been requested. Findings that suggest deterioration must be escalated through the local emergency pathway. Treatment amounts, medication doses, and timing instructions are intentionally omitted.

title: Synthetic pediatric DKA ongoing review and transfer checklist
text: Educational fixture only. Ongoing review records trends rather than isolated values. The handoff should summarize neurological observations, vital-sign trends, fluid balance, laboratory trends obtained under the local protocol, symptoms of deterioration, current interventions, consultations, and outstanding results. Any unexpected change prompts senior review and a documented escalation decision. When responsibility moves between teams or locations, use closed-loop communication: name the receiving clinician, state the current concerns, identify pending actions, invite questions, and record acceptance of the handoff. This fixture provides no treatment amounts, medication doses, or monitoring intervals.
